nodes.label: Phase 1 acceptance criteria
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Includes zero interactive elements below 44x44 measured in the DOM at 360 px, an IDOR probe returning 404, EXIF stripped from a geotagged fixture, and i18n gating the build.

nodes.label: Media upload hardening
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Magic-byte sniff, re-encode and EXIF strip on upload; gated serving with Content-Disposition and nosniff. Asserted against a geotagged fixture.

nodes.label: Phase 1 spec
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: F14 remainder (theme engine, feedback catalog, i18n), F1 exercise library and F8-lite admin, entered on a complete Phase 0.

nodes.label: Sequential jobs with explicit token budgets
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Jobs run sequentially because they share files and contracts; each carries inputs, working and reserve budgets, and a job that would exceed its input budget is split before it starts, never mid-run.
nodes.norm_label: sequential jobs with explicit token budgets

nodes.label: A notification whose subject is deleted
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Snapshot the text or resolve at read time and risk a dangling row; Phase 2 has a strong opinion about snapshots that must be applied or explicitly overruled.
nodes.norm_label: a notification whose subject is deleted

nodes.label: Architecture decisions are made before any DDL is written
nodes.source_location: The decisions this phase must make
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Getting them wrong is a 12-step table rebuild later because SQLite cannot alter a CHECK or an FK, so they are answered by a design plus adversarial-review pass the way migration 010 was.
nodes.norm_label: architecture decisions are made before any ddl is written

nodes.label: Quiet hours, server-side, with no cron
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Suppress at write time or filter at read time — each choice does something different to a notification that goes stale during the window.
nodes.norm_label: quiet hours, server-side, with no cron

nodes.label: Retention ENFORCED, not documented
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: There is no scheduler in this product, so something has to actually delete an old message rather than a document promising it.

nodes.label: Join flow A — invite link
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: The token must be unguessable and single-use unless declared multi.

nodes.label: Join flow C — pre-generated account
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: The client MUST be forced to change credentials on first login, or the coach retains access to their account forever.

nodes.label: Join flow B — team code
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: The code space must resist brute force: rate-limited per IP AND per code.

nodes.label: Phase 2 spec
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: F2 coach-client links and join flows, F11 onboarding, F3 plans, the guided player, logging and PRs.

nodes.label: Codes are CSPRNG, >=128 bits, compared in constant time
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Every redemption is audited, and expiry, max_uses and revocation are all enforced inside the UPDATE rather than checked before it.
nodes.norm_label: codes are csprng, >=128 bits, compared in constant time

nodes.label: Migration 008 — plans and logs
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: workout_plans, days, items, logs and log sets — the tables the J4 adversarial pass later reworked into migration 010.

nodes.label: Weight is stored in grams as an integer
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Floating-point kilos accumulate error across a year of logs and make 'is this a PR' a question about rounding; weights must round-trip exactly.
nodes.norm_label: weight is stored in grams as an integer

nodes.label: Migration 003 — exercise library
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Exercises plus an FTS5 external-content shadow kept in sync by three triggers; muscle_groups and equipment are lookup TABLES because they are admin-editable, and no JSON list ever stands in for a relation.

nodes.label: The visibility predicate is in SQL and a miss is 404
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: status = 'global' OR owner_id = @user, hardcoded on every exercise read with a narrow admin arm; an IDOR probe returns 404 because a 403 confirms the row exists.
nodes.norm_label: the visibility predicate is in sql and a miss is 404

nodes.label: The link is the authority
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: coach_clients carries the relationship, so archiving it withdraws access on the very next request because the predicate is in the SQL and not in a cached flag; chat and notifications hang off the link, never off a pair of user ids.

nodes.label: The Visual Design Bible outranks the design-intelligence skill
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: The recommended style was adopted only within the Bible's constraints and the mono third family was rejected under the two-family cap.
nodes.norm_label: the visual design bible outranks the design-intelligence skill

nodes.label: Phase 2 acceptance criteria
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Another coach's client id returns 404, an archived link loses access immediately, a replayed set-completion does not double-count a PR, and weights round-trip exactly.

nodes.label: Migration 006 — coaching
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: coach_clients, teams, invite_codes and referrals, with a UNIQUE on the pair and a composite index on (coach_id, status).

nodes.label: No WebSocket — chat polls
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: A socket needs a connection lifecycle, auth on upgrade and reconnect semantics, none of which earn their cost before there are two users talking; the upgrade path is documented, not built.

nodes.label: Migration 002 — theming
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: user_theme_prefs and element_style_config; the gradient is a genuine non-relational config blob, which is the one case the data-model rules allow JSON.

nodes.label: No message editing; deletion is a tombstone
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: A sent message is a fact.
nodes.norm_label: no message editing; deletion is a tombstone

nodes.label: No push notifications in v1; push_devices ships inert
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: FCM/APNs is a deployment concern with per-platform credentials; the table exists only so adding it later is not a migration.
nodes.norm_label: no push notifications in v1; push_devices ships inert

nodes.label: Phase 3 spec
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: F5 in-app notifications and F6 polled chat, plus the notification surface every later phase hangs its events off.

nodes.label: Every gate added must be proven load-bearing
nodes.author: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Broken deliberately once and seen to fail by name; a gate never seen to fail is not evidence.
nodes.norm_label: every gate added must be proven load-bearing

nodes.label: npm run check:worker-tx — 6 transaction bodies, no conditional return after a write
nodes.norm_label: npm run check:worker-tx — 6 transaction bodies, no conditional return after a write

nodes.label: copyDaysTx committed a refused copy (commit-on-return violation)
nodes.rationale: It grew a plan's cycle before checking destination slots; since the schedule is starts_on + k*cycle_days + day_index, a refused copy silently re-dated every future occurrence.
nodes.norm_label: copydaystx committed a refused copy (commit-on-return violation)

nodes.label: T1.42 — the worker-tx review item became a gate
nodes.rationale: A code-review checklist item that nobody runs is not a control; turning ADR-0005 clause 3 into npm run check:worker-tx found a live violation on its first run.
nodes.norm_label: t1.42 — the worker-tx review item became a gate

nodes.label: CUT 2 — cover replacement; changing a cover is DELETE then POST
nodes.rationale: Replace is the highest-defect verb in the corpus: one FATAL plus four severe, traded for one extra slot of the daily-40 budget.
nodes.norm_label: cut 2 — cover replacement; changing a cover is delete then post

nodes.label: The five attack lenses: forge / replay / race / IDOR / extremes
nodes.norm_label: the five attack lenses: forge / replay / race / idor / extremes

nodes.label: RACE-1 (FATAL) — updatePostMediaTx soft-deletes the cover then returns 'missing'
nodes.rationale: better-sqlite3 commits on return, so the coach's cover is destroyed while the API answers 404; the same shape was latent in all three designs and invisible to check-worker-tx.
nodes.norm_label: race-1 (fatal) — updatepostmediatx soft-deletes the cover then returns 'missing'

nodes.label: backend/scripts/check-worker-tx.mjs (clause 3 as a gate)
nodes.rationale: It found a live violation on its first run, and that bug outlived the full rebuild — which is the argument for gates over checklists in one sentence.

nodes.label: All error-producing validation runs BEFORE the first write; after a write the body may only complete
nodes.rationale: Guard-in-UPDATE patterns are unaffected: the guard lives in the SQL and a changes===0 probe is a read.
nodes.norm_label: all error-producing validation runs before the first write; after a write the body may only complete

nodes.label: 13-agent adversarial pass (4 readers, 3 stances, 5 lenses, 1 synthesis)
nodes.rationale: Three independent designs drawn under different stances — smallest-core, explicit-state-machine, attacker-first — then attacked, then synthesised.
nodes.norm_label: 13-agent adversarial pass (4 readers, 3 stances, 5 lenses, 1 synthesis)

nodes.label: ADR-0005 — Worker-tx law: a tx that returns, commits
nodes.rationale: better-sqlite3's .transaction() commits on return, so a validation error returned after a write persists the write while the client sees a 400. Only throw rolls back.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005 — worker-tx law: a tx that returns, commits

nodes.label: check:all — the composite gate
nodes.rationale: A probe that only runs when somebody remembers is a snapshot, not a gate.

nodes.label: trg_post_doc_needs_a_source_upd (replaces the body XOR trigger)
nodes.rationale: The XOR trigger refused ordinary edits and would have made the entire published corpus permanently uneditable the day doc_version was bumped.

nodes.label: backend/scripts/verify-022.mjs
nodes.rationale: Builds a throwaway DB from the real migrations and drives the real routes; the single fixture lie is time.

nodes.label: A gate never seen to fail is not evidence
nodes.rationale: Every closing gate was proven load-bearing by breaking the thing it guards and watching it fail by name.
nodes.norm_label: a gate never seen to fail is not evidence

nodes.label: THE BODY RULE — one producer, one consumer, one statement, one gate
nodes.rationale: body_src / body_doc / body_excerpt / doc_version must move together; no trigger can express 'is the parse of', so the derivation is a CODE control and the spec says so instead of asserting a control that was never built.
nodes.norm_label: the body rule — one producer, one consumer, one statement, one gate

nodes.label: Thirty assertions, each with a break that must be seen to fail
nodes.rationale: A clean result is a statement about coverage before it is a statement about the subject.
nodes.norm_label: thirty assertions, each with a break that must be seen to fail

nodes.label: The five evidence rules
nodes.rationale: A test never seen to fail is not evidence; a screenshot is evidence of a frame and a measurement is evidence of a fact; an audit run once is a snapshot and a gate is what keeps being true; an audit must not carry its own copy of what it audits; a path exercised one way is one untested branch from never having worked.

nodes.label: Evidence rule 6 — a probe never seen to fire cannot be told apart from a clean subject
nodes.rationale: Before recording a zero, plant the defect and watch the zero become a one.
nodes.norm_label: evidence rule 6 — a probe never seen to fire cannot be told apart from a clean subject

nodes.label: Webview E2E protocol
nodes.rationale: T7.5.3: the matrix cannot be filled without a device, so what shipped is the protocol — every row names a thing that behaves differently inside a webview, its file, and the evidence to capture.

nodes.label: An audit covers what it walks
nodes.rationale: /settings reported ten pure-black foregrounds that four previous phases had called clean because none had walked that route; the matrix now says ROUTES WALKED.
nodes.norm_label: an audit covers what it walks

nodes.label: The evidence rules, now seven
nodes.rationale: Rule 7 added: a clean result is a statement about coverage before it is a statement about the subject.

nodes.label: What this audit did NOT establish
nodes.rationale: Nothing about appearance, no gradient backgrounds, only main (fixed chrome excluded), eight screens, one theme and one language — stated so a clean row is not read as coverage it never had.
nodes.norm_label: what this audit did not establish

nodes.label: Gradients are invisible to this contrast measurement
nodes.rationale: backgroundColor on a gradient element is transparent, so the walk fell through to the dark card behind it; recorded rather than filtered, because the useful thing to hand the next runner is the limitation.
nodes.norm_label: gradients are invisible to this contrast measurement

nodes.label: The service worker must NOT be there in the native shell
nodes.rationale: A worker inside Capacitor caches URLs that do not change when the user installs a new version, so the app would update and appear not to; the unregister arm is the one that has never been exercised.
nodes.norm_label: the service worker must not be there in the native shell

nodes.label: Failed and not-tested are different marks
nodes.rationale: A matrix that quietly converts untested to a pass is worse than no matrix, because the next person reads it as coverage; each row also records device and OS version.
nodes.norm_label: failed and not-tested are different marks

nodes.label: The code is a better forwarding address than a document restating it
nodes.rationale: Lessons are distilled into cold notes because no code records them; gotchas are pruned once they are implemented with their reasoning in a comment beside the code, and each pruned line names its address.
nodes.norm_label: the code is a better forwarding address than a document restating it

nodes.label: The evidence rules, restated in hot memory
nodes.rationale: Seven rules; rule 4 was broken by its own author in Phase 5 and rule 7 was earned by a route four phases reported clean without walking it.
nodes.norm_label: the evidence rules, restated in hot memory

nodes.label: The hot/cold memory split
nodes.rationale: This file is a scratchpad for one phase; the Obsidian brain is the durable store that survives it. The coordinator syncs hot to cold at every phase approval and prunes the hot file back down.

nodes.label: post_media_mimes table
nodes.source_location: 2 columns, allowlist of media MIME types with an active flag

nodes.label: post_media table
nodes.source_location: 15 columns, webp-only media attached to coach posts with soft delete and write_uid idempotency

nodes.label: post_media_roles table
nodes.source_location: single-column key lookup (2 rows) constrained to lowercase a-z_ keys

nodes.label: public_policy table
nodes.source_location: 3 columns, key/value/note integer policy knobs (8 rows)

nodes.label: Phase 4 lessons
nodes.rationale: Distilled at the phase close so the hot working-memory file can be pruned; nutrition, health data and four second-implementations.

nodes.label: Phase 5 lessons
nodes.rationale: Money, and the audit that audited its own copy; distilled at the phase close.

nodes.label: J4 — the constraints migration 010 must satisfy
nodes.rationale: Distilled from three independent schema designs, each attacked from a security and a maintenance angle: 39 fatal flaws, 67 serious. The checklist the migration is not done until it answers.
nodes.norm_label: j4 — the constraints migration 010 must satisfy

nodes.label: SHARED_MEMORY — hot working memory
nodes.rationale: READ FIRST, WRITE LAST: the hot store of what the next job needs now, capped at ~2000 lines so it can always be read whole.

nodes.label: Careful handling of a known-hard edge is the tell
nodes.rationale: When a fiddly edge (an iOS limitation, an FTS metacharacter, a diacritic) is being handled carefully, somebody has been there already; care is evidence of prior art, not of rigour.
nodes.norm_label: careful handling of a known-hard edge is the tell

nodes.label: I keep writing the second implementation
nodes.rationale: Four times in one phase a solution was rewritten for a problem already solved in the repo, and three of the existing versions were better because they carried conditions the rewrite missed.
nodes.norm_label: i keep writing the second implementation

nodes.label: Machinery gets built; the two lines that call it do not
nodes.rationale: Migration 019 shipped the achievement catalogue, the table, the transaction and the ledger path, and nothing called any of it; the invocation is the whole difference between a system and a demo.
nodes.norm_label: machinery gets built; the two lines that call it do not

nodes.label: assertAdmin had three copies that had already drifted
nodes.rationale: An abuse-signal log line was added to one copy and reached neither of the others, so two of three refusals were still silent; a fourth copy was about to be written and got a shared note instead.
nodes.norm_label: assertadmin had three copies that had already drifted

nodes.label: A security predicate with two copies has one that is wrong
nodes.rationale: VISIBLE existed as a constant and as a hand-typed duplicate; extending one would have let a client open a prescribed exercise but not its picture. It now lives in one module with a visibleParams() helper, and the read predicate is deliberately one notch stricter than the write trigger.
nodes.norm_label: a security predicate with two copies has one that is wrong

nodes.label: Zero tap targets under 44x44, measured in the DOM
nodes.rationale: First confirmation that the floor holds in the rendered DOM rather than in the source; it lives in one place, the control recipe's min-h/min-w with no opt-out at the call site.
nodes.norm_label: zero tap targets under 44x44, measured in the dom

nodes.label: The control recipe
nodes.rationale: Every interactive element is built from it, so the 44px floor and all five interaction states are structural rather than remembered; density changes padding and type size only, never the hit area.

nodes.label: A control sized to its own graphic is the 44px bug in disguise
nodes.rationale: A checkbox rendering a 24px box became a 24px target; size the button to the floor and put the graphic inside it.
nodes.norm_label: a control sized to its own graphic is the 44px bug in disguise

nodes.label: Switch is a real role=switch with a 24px track in a 44px target
nodes.rationale: A screen reader says on/off rather than checked/unchecked, and only the first is true of a setting that takes effect immediately; the padding is transparent so the graphic stays the expected size while the target clears the floor.
nodes.norm_label: switch is a real role=switch with a 24px track in a 44px target

nodes.label: --target-min: 44px, both axes, no opt-out
nodes.rationale: The a11y floor lives in the base layer of every control variant rather than in anyone's memory, because the previous implementation lost it in twelve places.

nodes.label: trg_plan_source_owned_ins (the fatal finding)
nodes.rationale: The trigger requires source_plan_id to name a plan the SAME author wrote, so every template purchase — where a buyer receives a copy of a seller's plan — would have aborted.

nodes.label: Removing the surface beats guarding it
nodes.rationale: Instead of an SSRF guard on outbound USDA fetches, the importer reads a local file and the product ships no outbound HTTP client — which also makes food search work offline in a gym basement.
nodes.norm_label: removing the surface beats guarding it

nodes.label: Build less, and let the attack decide what
nodes.rationale: Three designs and five adversarial lenses produced 75 defects, thirteen of them unfixable afterwards because SQLite cannot alter a CHECK or an FK.
nodes.norm_label: build less, and let the attack decide what

nodes.label: The marketplace was deleted
nodes.rationale: Thirteen of the twenty-one fatal-and-severe findings sat in the marketplace, so deleting the feature removed thirteen defects without writing one fix.

nodes.label: Verify the agent's citation before you act on it
nodes.rationale: Not distrust: a plan built on an unverified line is a plan with one unverified line in its foundation. Three claims that changed the phase scope were checked line by line and all three held.
nodes.norm_label: verify the agent's citation before you act on it

nodes.label: The marketplace is cut to migration 020
nodes.rationale: Thirteen of the twenty-one fatal-and-severe findings sat there, including the one fatal trigger; deleting the feature removed thirteen defects without writing one fix, and that is the phase's main result rather than a shortfall.
nodes.norm_label: the marketplace is cut to migration 020

nodes.label: No markdown library and no sanitizer
nodes.rationale: ~330 lines, zero dependencies, 50 attacks; measured first — the frontend has zero HTML sinks. Depth is structural (block to li to inline), so a React renderer needs no depth prop.
nodes.norm_label: no markdown library and no sanitizer

nodes.label: The public predicate binds ZERO parameters
nodes.rationale: A pure function of the row, so a signed-in visitor gets byte-identical bytes to an anonymous one; held by a gate that greps the public routes for req.user and fails by file and line.
nodes.norm_label: the public predicate binds zero parameters

nodes.label: Copy-on-assign design
nodes.rationale: A template is a mould, never a live link: assigning deep-copies the plan and logging deep-copies the prescription.

nodes.label: History-integrity design
nodes.rationale: A log is a historical fact, not a view of current state.

nodes.label: Snapshot Session design
nodes.rationale: The session is a self-contained snapshot minted at start, so the player needs zero network and zero joins while the client trains.

nodes.label: Snapshots record what the WRITER saw, including the language
nodes.rationale: The snapshot took foods.name (canonical English), so a Hungarian user logged Zabpehely and their diary said Oats, rolled, dry; a row is a record of a past act, not a live view, so it never retranslates.
nodes.norm_label: snapshots record what the writer saw, including the language

nodes.label: COPY, DO NOT REFERENCE
nodes.rationale: Three designers with three different starting lenses reached one answer, which is the strongest signal in the exercise and the spine of the schema.

nodes.label: A language-dependent fetch needs the language in the URL AND the query key
nodes.rationale: No ?lang= falls back to the browser's Accept-Language; no lang in the cache key survives a fix to the first bug and makes that fix look broken. Verified by switching language with no reload.
nodes.norm_label: a language-dependent fetch needs the language in the url and the query key

nodes.label: A snapshot is a fallback, not a display value
nodes.rationale: exercise_name_snapshot exists so a log still renders after a rename or delete; reading it while the link is live froze the plan in one language. The chain is requested, default, canonical, then snapshot.
nodes.norm_label: a snapshot is a fallback, not a display value

nodes.label: The measurement vocabulary is a reference TABLE with an FK
nodes.rationale: Not CHECK (metric IN (...)): adding 'forearm' a year from now is an INSERT, and a plausible-range bound that excludes a real person is an UPDATE.
nodes.norm_label: the measurement vocabulary is a reference table with an fk

nodes.label: No Atwater CHECK on foods
nodes.rationale: 4*protein+4*carb+9*fat ~ kcal is tempting and wrong; the seed proved it — beer, wine (ethanol is 7 kcal/g) and ground paprika (fibre) fired immediately, so the generator reports outliers instead of enforcing them.

nodes.label: A wrong CHECK is a 12-step table rebuild
nodes.rationale: SQLite cannot alter a CHECK or an FK, so a constraint chosen wrongly is unfixable in place; established by migration 013 and applied twice in advance in Phase 4.
nodes.norm_label: a wrong check is a 12-step table rebuild

nodes.label: Type-affinity traps
nodes.rationale: INTEGER is affinity, not a type, so a REAL sails through BETWEEN 1 AND 100; and a CHECK validating a value against a formula chosen by a column the writer also supplies is self-disabling.

nodes.label: The ach:<id> idempotency key defect
nodes.rationale: Five characters against an eight-character floor; fixed in the migration comment and in verify-019's own copy of the SQL, left wrong in the worker, so the probe went green over a production path that aborted on every unlock.

nodes.label: The audit carried its own copy of what it audits
nodes.rationale: Evidence rule four broken by its own author: where a probe must hold a copy, the copy has to be labelled as one and something else has to exercise the real path.
nodes.norm_label: the audit carried its own copy of what it audits

nodes.label: Fire-and-forget belongs at the CALL site
nodes.rationale: Where the decision is visible and the failure is logged; both defects of this phase surfaced only because the evaluator logged its failure instead of dying quietly.
nodes.norm_label: fire-and-forget belongs at the call site

nodes.label: The smoke suite exercises the real path
nodes.rationale: A schema probe that carries its own SQL can be attacked without a server, but something else must run the shipped code, or the green result describes the copy.
nodes.norm_label: the smoke suite exercises the real path

nodes.label: A catch that turns an error into a plausible value
nodes.rationale: .catch(() => ({ n: 0 })) around a query with a wrong column name reported a number indistinguishable from 'no records yet'. That is not resilience; it is a defect given somewhere to hide.
nodes.norm_label: a catch that turns an error into a plausible value

nodes.label: The autosave probe had already drifted from the hook
nodes.rationale: Its transcription called save(payload) while the shipped hook calls save(), so the central assertion exercised a signature that does not ship — rule 4 biting in the file that warns about rule 4.
nodes.norm_label: the autosave probe had already drifted from the hook

nodes.label: Smoke suites are hermetic
nodes.rationale: A throwaway server on a random port with a fresh temp database; the functional suite skips limiters and the limiters get their own run where the skip is not active, because rate limiters make a non-hermetic auth suite unrepeatable for 15 minutes.

nodes.label: Join codes are stored as sha256 hashes
nodes.rationale: The plaintext is returned exactly once, at creation, and exists nowhere else; listing codes never echoes it.
nodes.norm_label: join codes are stored as sha256 hashes

nodes.label: must_change_credentials locks a pre-generated account
nodes.rationale: Everything except /auth/me, /auth/change-credentials and /auth/logout is refused, enforced in requireAuth rather than per route.

nodes.label: Webview E2E probe (overflow, targets, one h1, alt, landmarks)
nodes.norm_label: webview e2e probe (overflow, targets, one h1, alt, landmarks)

nodes.label: OQ-5 — the Browser pane does not composite frames
nodes.norm_label: oq-5 — the browser pane does not composite frames

nodes.label: Webview E2E protocol — written, matrix blocked on a device
nodes.norm_label: webview e2e protocol — written, matrix blocked on a device

nodes.label: The measurable half is measured, the visual half is named as uncovered
nodes.norm_label: the measurable half is measured, the visual half is named as uncovered

nodes.label: Evidence rule 2 — a screenshot is evidence of a frame, a measurement of a fact
nodes.norm_label: evidence rule 2 — a screenshot is evidence of a frame, a measurement of a fact

nodes.label: Auth — jose access JWT 15 min + rotating refresh + argon2id
nodes.norm_label: auth — jose access jwt 15 min + rotating refresh + argon2id

nodes.label: Backend scaffold (Piscina SQLCipher worker pool, WAL pragmas)
nodes.norm_label: backend scaffold (piscina sqlcipher worker pool, wal pragmas)

nodes.label: src/lib/api.ts — typed ApiError, single-flight refresh, X-CSRF
nodes.norm_label: src/lib/api.ts — typed apierror, single-flight refresh, x-csrf

nodes.label: disabled_at — eight readers and nothing could set it
nodes.norm_label: disabled_at — eight readers and nothing could set it

nodes.label: Encrypted backup via VACUUM INTO + restore drill
nodes.norm_label: encrypted backup via vacuum into + restore drill

nodes.label: rekey.mjs — PRAGMA rekey refuses WAL, so the runbook switches modes
nodes.norm_label: rekey.mjs — pragma rekey refuses wal, so the runbook switches modes

nodes.label: The client never sends a macro
nodes.rationale: INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM foods copies macros from the server's own row in the same statement; sending one is a 400, not an ignore.
nodes.norm_label: the client never sends a macro

nodes.label: Macros are integers in a fixed scale, never REAL
nodes.rationale: Summing 40 floats against a target is how a day reads 1999.9999 against 2000.
nodes.norm_label: macros are integers in a fixed scale, never real

nodes.label: Totals are never stored
nodes.rationale: A day's kcal is SUM() at read time; a stored total is a number a client could eventually talk the server into writing, and a rollup is a second copy of a fact.

nodes.label: Streaks are computed, never stored
nodes.rationale: Ending YESTERDAY counts; a stored counter needs a nightly job to break it and is wrong every hour that job is late.

nodes.label: GET /admin/marketplace/reports authorised from the JWT alone
nodes.rationale: A revoked admin could read the moderation queue for up to fifteen minutes; its two sibling writes were fine because they re-check under the write lock.
nodes.norm_label: get /admin/marketplace/reports authorised from the jwt alone

nodes.label: Access JWT plus rotating opaque refresh token
nodes.rationale: 15-minute HS256 access token with sub/role/sv/jti claims; refresh is 32 random bytes stored as sha256, rotated every use, with a family_id per login.
nodes.norm_label: access jwt plus rotating opaque refresh token

nodes.label: An alias hid three admin routes from check-admin-audit
nodes.rationale: const requireAdmin = requireRole('admin') put three routes outside every rule in the gate; it reported 10 admin routes over a codebase with 15.
nodes.norm_label: an alias hid three admin routes from check-admin-audit

nodes.label: A coverage figure next to an OK is the first thing to read
nodes.rationale: Three gates shipped that phase had a blind spot and each printed the number that would have shown it: 0 inspected, 10 admin routes, 16 files use an inset.
nodes.norm_label: a coverage figure next to an ok is the first thing to read

nodes.label: Refresh reuse detection with a 10 s benign-race window
nodes.rationale: A consumed token replayed after 10 s revokes the family and bumps session_version; within 10 s it is 409 refresh in progress with no alarm, because that is two tabs racing rather than theft.
nodes.norm_label: refresh reuse detection with a 10 s benign-race window

nodes.label: The sv cache is 30 s and must be invalidated in the same operation
nodes.rationale: Anything that changes a role, disables a user or forces logout must bump session_version and call invalidateSvCache(userId) together, or the old token keeps working.
nodes.norm_label: the sv cache is 30 s and must be invalidated in the same operation

nodes.label: Coach food-log visibility deliberately not built
nodes.rationale: It needs the same explicit consent design the measurement shares got; 'coaching seems to imply it' is not a reason.
nodes.norm_label: coach food-log visibility deliberately not built

nodes.label: Four conditions in ONE share predicate
nodes.rationale: Share row exists, the specific flag is set, it is not revoked, and the link is still active; without the fourth, a coach who leaves keeps reading somebody's body photographs forever.
nodes.norm_label: four conditions in one share predicate

nodes.label: Health data changes the default, and the default is nobody
nodes.rationale: Every other feature answers 'may this coach see this' with 'yes while the link is active'; for measurements and photos the answer is only what the client explicitly shared.
nodes.norm_label: health data changes the default, and the default is nobody

nodes.label: Every photo read is logged before the bytes go out
nodes.rationale: A stream that fails halfway was still a look, and a log of completed transfers can be defeated by disconnecting; the viewer's email is snapshot so the answer survives account deletion.
nodes.norm_label: every photo read is logged before the bytes go out

nodes.label: Two consent flags rather than one
nodes.rationale: Waist measurement and body photographs are different consents; a single toggle forces the more sensitive one to ride along with the less.
nodes.norm_label: two consent flags rather than one

nodes.label: 403 is for roles, 404 is for objects
nodes.rationale: 'You are not a coach' reveals nothing about any object and is the one deliberate exception to 404-never-403; a real coach past the role gate must not learn another coach's link exists. The smoke suite tests both callers, because testing one is how the drift survived.
nodes.norm_label: 403 is for roles, 404 is for objects

nodes.label: coach_clients is the link, never a column on users
nodes.rationale: A client may be coached by different coaches over time; UNIQUE on (coach_id, client_id) and a trigger forbids self-coaching.
nodes.norm_label: coach_clients is the link, never a column on users

nodes.label: The balance has exactly one representation
nodes.rationale: A cache of SUM(ledger) written only by a recompute trigger; the rejected running-balance-per-row alternative bricks an account permanently once the two representations diverge. Loud-and-recoverable beats elegant-and-bricked.
nodes.norm_label: the balance has exactly one representation

nodes.label: Non-negativity is a TRIGGER on the ledger INSERT
nodes.rationale: On the wallet it would also fire from a cascade, and a user whose credit is deleted before their debit would momentarily recompute negative and abort their own account deletion.
nodes.norm_label: non-negativity is a trigger on the ledger insert

nodes.label: A cache may accelerate a read; it may never be the source of the comparison that creates it
nodes.rationale: PR detection compared against a record cache the same transaction then updated, so the number of PRs — and later of coins — depended on network delivery order. Derive PRs from the set rows.
nodes.norm_label: a cache may accelerate a read; it may never be the source of the comparison that creates it

nodes.label: Warm-up sets poisoning the record book
nodes.rationale: One design filtered warm-ups in the PR layer and nowhere else, so they still moved top weight, total reps and the records upsert.
nodes.norm_label: warm-up sets poisoning the record book

nodes.label: Optimistic send — a failed bubble stays marked, never vanishes
nodes.norm_label: optimistic send — a failed bubble stays marked, never vanishes

nodes.label: Polling contract — 5s open, 60s badge, paused when hidden
nodes.norm_label: polling contract — 5s open, 60s badge, paused when hidden

nodes.label: Zero horizontal overflow at 360 and 1440
nodes.rationale: scrollWidth - clientWidth per route after navigation settled: 0 px on ten routes at 360 and twelve at 1440.

nodes.label: The probe had to prove it navigated
nodes.rationale: Ten zeroes is exactly what a probe that never left the first screen returns; the re-run captured a distinct heading and content length per route, so the zeroes are about ten screens rather than one screen ten times.
nodes.norm_label: the probe had to prove it navigated

nodes.label: Distinguish a scrolling ancestor from a clipped one
nodes.rationale: Elements 101 px past the edge were inside an overflow-x:auto section rail — reachable by scrolling, which is what a rail is for; had the ancestor been overflow:hidden it would have been a real defect.
nodes.norm_label: distinguish a scrolling ancestor from a clipped one

nodes.label: Haptics are silently absent on iOS
nodes.rationale: navigator.vibrate does not exist on iOS Safari at all, so the Capacitor plugin is the only path; the failure mode to watch for is no buzz AND no error.
nodes.norm_label: haptics are silently absent on ios

nodes.label: iOS starts every AudioContext suspended
nodes.rationale: A user gesture must resume it; the interesting case is backgrounding during a rest interval, because iOS may suspend the context again.

nodes.label: Speech cue voices differ per platform and language
nodes.rationale: Hungarian is the likely gap; record WHICH failure occurs, because silent is worse than wrong-accent and the two need different fixes.
nodes.norm_label: speech cue voices differ per platform and language

nodes.label: Safe-area insets on real hardware
nodes.rationale: The static gate holds every edge-pinned element to its inset but cannot see the rendered result; landscape matters because a phone propped against a rack is how somebody reads their next set.

nodes.label: .screen-x uses max(), never addition
nodes.rationale: The safe-area inset replaces the gutter when it is larger, so an edge never gets 16px stacked on top of a 44px cutout; a fitness app is used sideways, and check-safe-area reads this exact shape.

nodes.label: viewport-fit=cover
nodes.rationale: Lets the layout reach the physical screen edges, which is what makes the safe-area inset tokens meaningful.

nodes.label: Migration 018 — the live erasure blocker
nodes.rationale: audit_log.actor_id is ON DELETE SET NULL and the append-only trigger had no WHEN clause, so an FK action — which IS an UPDATE to a trigger — aborted deletion for anyone who had ever produced an audit row.

nodes.label: History never cascades
nodes.rationale: Deleting a coach account would have erased clients' training history through a chain of ON DELETE CASCADE, and no later migration can change an FK action. A log row keeps its own copy of what it needs.

nodes.label: audit_log is append-only by trigger, not by convention
nodes.rationale: BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers enforce it, so no code path — including a careless maintenance script — can rewrite history.
nodes.norm_label: audit_log is append-only by trigger, not by convention

nodes.label: The migration runner silently skips a duplicate number
nodes.rationale: Both critics caught that 009 was already taken because the roster landed while the designs were being attacked; the runner should refuse a duplicate rather than skip it.
nodes.norm_label: the migration runner silently skips a duplicate number

nodes.label: The migration runner keeps a ledger, not just user_version
nodes.rationale: Gating on user_version alone meant a reserved number written after a later one would be skipped forever and silently; out-of-order files now apply and are logged at warn. The fix's own bug was caught by running it.
nodes.norm_label: the migration runner keeps a ledger, not just user_version

nodes.label: Migration numbering and the in-file user_version bump
nodes.rationale: The file number is the target user_version and the bump happens inside the file's own transaction, so a half-applied migration cannot claim the version.
nodes.norm_label: migration numbering and the in-file user_version bump

nodes.label: No follower count, and its absence is the design
nodes.norm_label: no follower count, and its absence is the design

nodes.label: coach_follows — private, no count, no ranking influence
nodes.norm_label: coach_follows — private, no count, no ranking influence

nodes.label: The void is idempotent without a write_uid
nodes.norm_label: the void is idempotent without a write_uid

nodes.label: A void is a THIRD state — rendered WITHDRAWN
nodes.norm_label: a void is a third state — rendered withdrawn

nodes.label: Body charts are direction="neutral"
nodes.rationale: The app does not know whether +3 kg is a bulk going well or a month going badly, and a green number answers that on somebody's behalf.

nodes.label: A macro bar clamps its fill, never its label
nodes.rationale: Past the target it turns warning, not danger — someone 300 kcal over has had a normal Tuesday.
nodes.norm_label: a macro bar clamps its fill, never its label

nodes.label: An assertion ships with a control that proves it is not vacuous
nodes.rationale: verify-autosave had eight assertions about the race and none about the moment before it; it now carries the case and a control showing that without the seed the same untouched document does save.
nodes.norm_label: an assertion ships with a control that proves it is not vacuous

nodes.label: Opening any existing post fired an unrequested PUT
nodes.rationale: savedSnapshot starts null, so the hook saw a difference between screen and last-saved and PUT a post nobody touched 1.5s later; one line seeds the snapshot from the loaded post.
nodes.norm_label: opening any existing post fired an unrequested put

nodes.label: The offline outbox on a real dead network
nodes.rationale: The logic is proved 31/31; this tests the wiring — force-quit while offline, relaunch, restore the network, then verify on the SERVER, because the client showing 'sent' is not evidence.
nodes.norm_label: the offline outbox on a real dead network

nodes.label: Out-of-order arrival is not the same problem as replay
nodes.rationale: Every idempotency story proved resending an identical payload is safe and then assumed that is all an offline queue does; twelve queued set-checks arrive interleaved and duplicated.
nodes.norm_label: out-of-order arrival is not the same problem as replay

nodes.label: Two font families, self-hosted
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted via @fontsource so the strict CSP never has to allow a third-party font origin; the display face is opt-in per element because setting it on body copy is the fastest way to make an app look like a poster.

nodes.label: ADR-0005 commit-on-return
nodes.rationale: better-sqlite3 commits a transaction when the wrapped function returns, which bounds what a single worker transaction can promise.

nodes.label: syncOfflineQueue was structurally unimplementable
nodes.rationale: It promised one immediate transaction, per-op results and a throw on a bad op; under better-sqlite3's commit-on-return law you can have any two.

nodes.label: A denormalised id gets BEFORE INSERT and BEFORE UPDATE triggers, or it does not exist
nodes.rationale: All three designs denormalised an owner or parent id for query speed and left at least one unguarded — a cross-tenant write reachable from the lowest-privilege role.
nodes.norm_label: a denormalised id gets before insert and before update triggers, or it does not exist

nodes.label: Every ownership-bearing INSERT is INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE
nodes.rationale: Ownership predicates were written for the UPDATE path and assumed for INSERT, but INSERT ... VALUES admits no guard, so a coach could inject a plan into a stranger's client.
nodes.norm_label: every ownership-bearing insert is insert ... select ... where

nodes.label: B11 — the optimistic rollback was designed and never wired
nodes.rationale: onMutate returns a previous-state context nothing ever reads, so a failed send leaves a phantom bubble until the 5s poll — which also fails when the failure was the network — while the composer already holds the same text.
nodes.norm_label: b11 — the optimistic rollback was designed and never wired

nodes.label: Assert the property, not a datum that names a category
nodes.rationale: Enabling German silently stopped two older tests from testing anything, because they had used 'de' as their example of a disabled language and hardcoded the language list.
nodes.norm_label: assert the property, not a datum that names a category

nodes.label: Reference data belongs in a migration, not an import script
nodes.rationale: A freshly migrated and a seeded database had different language tables and nothing said so. ROSTER (which languages exist) is schema; ENABLED (which may be served) is a runtime policy flag.
nodes.norm_label: reference data belongs in a migration, not an import script

nodes.label: Sync the brain before the context window runs low
nodes.rationale: Owner instruction: anything unsynced when context is lost is simply gone, and a changed detail is updated in the same breath rather than letting the vault describe an older version of the code.
nodes.norm_label: sync the brain before the context window runs low

nodes.label: The brain data-model and API notes are generated
nodes.rationale: Derived from the live schema and the mounted routers by npm run brain:gen; hand-written versions were stale within a day.
nodes.norm_label: the brain data-model and api notes are generated

nodes.label: Checkout Session creation — NOT built
nodes.rationale: The outbound half of billing; blocked on live Stripe credentials unavailable in this environment

nodes.label: Coach subscription billing (webhook handler half)
nodes.rationale: The webhook HANDLER that owns subscription state is done and verified 29/29; the outbound half — creating the Checkout Session — is not built because it needs live Stripe credentials this environment does not have

nodes.label: FREE tier cap of 3 — placeholder, not a decision
nodes.rationale: Explicitly flagged as the owner placeholder value, still open (see note in migration 026)
nodes.norm_label: free tier cap of 3 — placeholder, not a decision

nodes.label: 15-minute access JWT with a kid keyring
nodes.norm_label: 15-minute access jwt with a kid keyring

nodes.label: storage/media — re-encoded assets with random keys
nodes.norm_label: storage/media — re-encoded assets with random keys

nodes.label: Numbered migrations keyed to PRAGMA user_version (ADR-0001)
nodes.rationale: The file number IS the target user_version and the bump happens inside the file own transaction, so a crash mid-file rolls the version back with it
nodes.norm_label: numbered migrations keyed to pragma user_version (adr-0001)

nodes.label: Piscina worker pool (all database access)
nodes.rationale: Only src/db/index.js is imported by the app and only src/db/worker.js opens a connection

nodes.label: Rotating opaque refresh tokens with family reuse detection
nodes.rationale: Backed by a session_version kill-switch that invalidates a users live sessions
nodes.norm_label: rotating opaque refresh tokens with family reuse detection

nodes.label: Security posture — OWASP ASVS L2 aligned
nodes.norm_label: security posture — owasp asvs l2 aligned

nodes.label: Strict CSP without unsafe-inline (+ HSTS, frame-ancestors none, exact-origin CORS)
nodes.rationale: The pre-paint theme script ships as a sha256 hash so no inline script allowance is needed
nodes.norm_label: strict csp without unsafe-inline (+ hsts, frame-ancestors none, exact-origin cors)

nodes.label: storage/tmp — upload quarantine with hourly sweep
nodes.norm_label: storage/tmp — upload quarantine with hourly sweep

nodes.label: brain-gen.mjs — data-model doc generator
nodes.rationale: backend/scripts/brain-gen.mjs writes the ERD and every table note from the LIVE schema and the mounted routers; the notes are never hand-edited (npm run brain:gen)

nodes.label: FTS5 shadow search tables
nodes.rationale: coach_posts_fts, exercise_translations_fts, food_translations_fts and foods_fts keep full-text search inside SQLite instead of an external index

nodes.label: TRACKER system architecture
nodes.rationale: React 19 SPA (Capacitor-wrapped) talks same-origin with HttpOnly cookies to an Express 5 API; every database call goes through a Piscina worker pool onto an encrypted SQLite file

nodes.label: TRACKER data model (schema version 25)
nodes.rationale: 81 tables plus 4 FTS5 shadow tables, generated from the live schema

nodes.label: Per-coach client seat cap tied to subscription tier
nodes.rationale: Enforced at "add a client", NEVER at "have clients" — a tier can drop without consent (a failed card), so a billing event must not dissolve an existing relationship. Both link paths are guarded (redeemInviteTx and the rewritten pregenerateClientTx); verify:seats 20/20, each guard mutation-proven
nodes.norm_label: per-coach client seat cap tied to subscription tier

nodes.label: Coach resolution chain: subscription → customer → Checkout metadata
nodes.rationale: Each fallback step is verified against the users table and never trusted as supplied — a metadata hint naming somebody else cannot move an existing subscription
nodes.norm_label: coach resolution chain: subscription → customer → checkout metadata

nodes.label: 5-pass adversarial checklist (forge / replay / race / IDOR / extremes)
nodes.rationale: Run against POST /payments/webhook, 31/31. The probe STATES its coverage (1 endpoint) rather than implying all. RACE and IDOR were previously unmeasured: two concurrent deliveries apply exactly once, and a metadata hint naming somebody else cannot move an existing subscription
nodes.norm_label: 5-pass adversarial checklist (forge / replay / race / idor / extremes)

nodes.label: Inbound webhook hardening
nodes.rationale: Raw-body constant-time HMAC verify, replay bounded on BOTH timestamp and event id, verify-then-parse enforced structurally (JSON.parse appears once, below the check, nothing between). Mounted above express.json (the signature covers raw bytes) and above csrfProtection (Stripe sends no cookie — the signature IS the authentication, and it is stronger). Every failure answers an identical bare 400. verify:webhook 24/24

nodes.label: Subscription status map fails CLOSED
nodes.rationale: An unknown provider status maps to canceled rather than to an entitled state

nodes.label: Tier↔price mapping stored as DATA (migration 028)
nodes.rationale: The tier/price relationship lives in the database, not in code branches

nodes.label: Out-of-order guard on provider_event_at
nodes.rationale: A late-arriving older webhook must not overwrite newer subscription state

nodes.label: Law: the build refuses design-token drift (check-tokens)
nodes.rationale: check-tokens fails the build on a raw colour, radius, duration, off-grid spacing, a sub-44px control, or a hand-rolled <button> outside the primitives folder
nodes.norm_label: law: the build refuses design-token drift (check-tokens)

nodes.label: Law: the client is never trusted about anything
nodes.rationale: Not a price, not a role, not a file type, not its own language header. Uploads are sniffed from magic bytes and re-encoded, the accent contrast guard re-runs server-side, status and owner_id are never accepted from a request body
nodes.norm_label: law: the client is never trusted about anything

nodes.label: Law: nothing touches the database off the worker pool
nodes.rationale: better-sqlite3 is synchronous by design, so a Promise wrapped around a sync call moves nothing off the event loop — only a real worker thread does
nodes.norm_label: law: nothing touches the database off the worker pool

nodes.label: Law: guards live inside the UPDATE
nodes.rationale: A guard in a preceding SELECT lets two racing requests both win; anything with a branch gets a named worker function, writeTx is for simple writes only
nodes.norm_label: law: guards live inside the update

nodes.label: Law: an ownership miss answers 404, never 403
nodes.rationale: A 403 confirms the id is real, which is enough to enumerate another coach private library; a row you may not see must be indistinguishable from one that does not exist
nodes.norm_label: law: an ownership miss answers 404, never 403

nodes.label: Law: routes are thin
nodes.rationale: Validate with a .strict() zod schema, authorize, make one worker call, shape the response. No SQL lives in a route file

nodes.label: Coin ledger idempotency key
nodes.rationale: idempotency_key is NOT NULL and carries a unique index (coin_ledger_idem_uidx), so a retried coin movement can never be applied twice

nodes.label: @theme static is required in the primitive token layer
nodes.rationale: Tailwind 4 tree-shakes unused theme vars, and half this layer is consumed through var() from JS, so without static those variables resolve to the empty string.
nodes.norm_label: @theme static is required in the primitive token layer

nodes.label: @theme static is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: Tailwind tree-shakes theme variables it sees no utility for, and half this layer is consumed through var() from CSS and JS, so without static the durations, easings, icon sizes and column widths silently resolve to the empty string.

nodes.label: tokens.css is the only file allowed a raw value
nodes.rationale: No raw color, radius or duration anywhere else in the frontend; the build gate enforces it.
nodes.norm_label: tokens.css is the only file allowed a raw value

nodes.label: tokens.css is the only file permitted a raw value
nodes.rationale: index.css is deliberately NOT exempt — it is linted like a feature file and additionally read as input by three gates. Two escape hatches exist and both require a written reason.
nodes.norm_label: tokens.css is the only file permitted a raw value

nodes.label: max(ratio vs black, ratio vs white) >= 4.5 is vacuous
nodes.rationale: Those two curves cross at 4.58, so the better of the pair never drops below 4.5 for any colour; the binding constraint is the accent AS TEXT on the app background.
nodes.norm_label: max(ratio vs black, ratio vs white) >= 4.5 is vacuous

nodes.label: checkAccent tests accent-as-text-on-surface, not fg-on-accent
nodes.rationale: The obvious check is vacuous: those two contrast curves cross at 4.58, so the better of the pair never fails.

nodes.label: npm run build — check-tokens + check-i18n + check-interval + tsc + vite
nodes.norm_label: npm run build — check-tokens + check-i18n + check-interval + tsc + vite

nodes.label: Element feedback variants E1–E26 (five variants each)
nodes.rationale: The active variant is a GLOBAL admin-switchable setting applied to every user with no redeploy; the variant changes how a control FEELS, never whether it works.
nodes.norm_label: element feedback variants e1–e26 (five variants each)

nodes.label: /playground — every element against all five variants at once
nodes.rationale: Parity with the database is a smoke check, so the UI cannot offer a variant the DB rejects.
nodes.norm_label: /playground — every element against all five variants at once

nodes.label: useElementVariant('EN') hook
nodes.rationale: Components never hardcode behaviour — they ask for the active variant and render accordingly.

nodes.label: ElementStyleProvider — variant map with localStorage cache and atomic swap
nodes.norm_label: elementstyleprovider — variant map with localstorage cache and atomic swap

nodes.label: Bottom sheets — Escape closes, focus enters on open, softer spring
nodes.norm_label: bottom sheets — escape closes, focus enters on open, softer spring

nodes.label: CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K, desktop only)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not animated — anything used 100x a day is in the 'no animation, ever' row.

nodes.label: lib/haptics — Capacitor on device, a genuine no-op on web
nodes.rationale: A wrong buzz is worse than none, and the Vibration API is not a substitute.
nodes.norm_label: lib/haptics — capacitor on device, a genuine no-op on web

nodes.label: OfflineIndicator
nodes.rationale: It disappears only after a real request reaches /healthz, because navigator.onLine is honest about 'no interface' and lies about captive portals.

nodes.label: Not built: a queued-action store for offline writes
nodes.rationale: The indicator reports the state; it does not yet hold a queue.
nodes.norm_label: not built: a queued-action store for offline writes

nodes.label: Pull to refresh — only arms at scroll top
nodes.norm_label: pull to refresh — only arms at scroll top

nodes.label: Skeletons, never spinners (ScreenSkeleton)
nodes.rationale: Shapes match the real geometry, so the swap causes no layout shift.

nodes.label: Swipe actions — pointer capture, damping past the threshold
nodes.norm_label: swipe actions — pointer capture, damping past the threshold

nodes.label: Toasts — aria-live polite, auto-dismiss pauses under the cursor
nodes.norm_label: toasts — aria-live polite, auto-dismiss pauses under the cursor

nodes.label: UX base pack — cross-screen behaviour built once in the shell
nodes.norm_label: ux base pack — cross-screen behaviour built once in the shell

nodes.label: prefers-reduced-motion: the state change still HAPPENS, it just does not travel
nodes.rationale: A global CSS backstop collapses durations and components branch on useMotionSafe so JS-driven springs do not move either.
nodes.norm_label: prefers-reduced-motion: the state change still happens, it just does not travel

nodes.label: Every control keeps its accessible name, 44x44 floor and focus ring regardless of variant
nodes.norm_label: every control keeps its accessible name, 44x44 floor and focus ring regardless of variant

nodes.label: Untestable in this environment: autofocus, animation end-states, screenshots
nodes.rationale: Neither claimed working nor reported broken.
nodes.norm_label: untestable in this environment: autofocus, animation end-states, screenshots

nodes.label: Three cue channels, never one 'sounds' switch
nodes.rationale: navigator.vibrate does not exist on iOS Safari, so bundling the beep with the voice silently costs that user every non-visual cue they have.
nodes.norm_label: three cue channels, never one 'sounds' switch

nodes.label: I wrote the second implementation, and it was the worse one
nodes.rationale: A limitation you find yourself documenting carefully is a strong signal that someone already hit it — look for their answer before writing your own.
nodes.norm_label: i wrote the second implementation, and it was the worse one

nodes.label: The strings nobody looks at: sr-only text, dead i18n keys, a check whose subject moved
nodes.rationale: A check whose subject moved does not fail — it passes, quietly, forever.
nodes.norm_label: the strings nobody looks at: sr-only text, dead i18n keys, a check whose subject moved

nodes.label: D-P1 — no PVP, Opus fills every role solo
nodes.norm_label: d-p1 — no pvp, opus fills every role solo

nodes.label: Phase 8 — later bucket (health sync, payment processor)
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 — later bucket (health sync, payment processor)

nodes.label: The compiler as a reviewer
nodes.rationale: Wiring the last tab narrowed the union to never and the 'arrives in phase N' placeholder stopped compiling; arrange for a type system to watch placeholders where it is cheap.

nodes.label: The importer's counter is computed by difference
nodes.rationale: An upsert reports changes = 1 either way, so a per-row check reports 'all new' on every re-import; a number that is always the flattering one is not a measurement.
nodes.norm_label: the importer's counter is computed by difference

nodes.label: The reason decides the movement
nodes.rationale: Direction and ceiling are DATA, so 'spend a negative amount to mint' is unrepresentable rather than refused, and a new movement type is an INSERT.

nodes.label: Stripe MCP connector present but not authorized
nodes.rationale: No live API access from a non-interactive session; the integration can be written without it, only live calls and account inspection need it.
nodes.norm_label: stripe mcp connector present but not authorized

nodes.label: acceptGuidelinesTx
nodes.rationale: INSERT OR IGNORE on the natural key; OR REPLACE is forbidden because the row is append-only evidence.

nodes.label: DELETE /compose/posts/:publicId/cover
nodes.rationale: Soft-deletes; the bytes stay on disk, because a soft delete that hard-deletes bytes cannot be undone.

nodes.label: Eleven named worker transactions (no writeTx in this feature)
nodes.rationale: Every write has a guard, a branch or an audit row paired with a changes===0 probe, which the generic writeTx cannot do.
nodes.norm_label: eleven named worker transactions (no writetx in this feature)

nodes.label: Phase 7 — the coach-side composer
nodes.rationale: The write surface for the public marketplace shipped in Phase 6: migration 022, 5 new backend files, 8 new frontend files, 11 named worker transactions.

nodes.label: POST /compose/guidelines/accept
nodes.rationale: Without this route every publish in the product is denied; the client echoes the version it displayed, it does not choose it.

nodes.label: POST /compose/posts/:publicId/publish
nodes.rationale: quota_reached is 409, not 429 — it is a business rule, and every 429 in this product comes from express-rate-limit.

nodes.label: POST /compose/posts/:publicId/restore
nodes.rationale: Withdraw being irreversible while permanently consuming a quota slot is a worse product than a gated restore.

nodes.label: POST /compose/preview
nodes.rationale: Writes nothing, reads nothing, and runs the same buildBody the write path uses so preview and published page are the same function of the same input.

nodes.label: POST /compose/profile/unpublish
nodes.rationale: No standing gate, deliberately — a coach who has lost standing must still be able to take themselves down.

nodes.label: publishPostTx
nodes.rationale: The object is looked up FIRST, before anything is said about the caller.

nodes.label: PUT /compose/posts/:publicId (edit)
nodes.rationale: ONE statement, no branch; all four body columns are always in the SET list.

nodes.label: PUT /compose/profile (edit)
nodes.rationale: PUT, not PATCH: every field is required and null means cleared, which removes absent-vs-null merge semantics entirely.

nodes.label: row_version — monotonic optimistic concurrency counter
nodes.rationale: unixepoch() is one-second granular, so a timestamp guard silently no-ops inside its own second and reports a false conflict on retry; a counter cannot collide.

nodes.label: trg_post_restore_standing_upd
nodes.rationale: Restore is a publication event and no 021 trigger watched it, so a coach who never accepted the guidelines now in force could return a whole withdrawn back catalogue to the anonymous surface.

nodes.label: updateCoachProfileTx
nodes.rationale: Specialty and city membership are checked before the DELETE, because after it a conditional return would COMMIT a profile stripped of its specialties.

nodes.label: write_uid — owner-scoped idempotency inside the guard's own uniqueness constraint
nodes.rationale: House form: a column inside a UNIQUE index, never an idempotency_keys table.
nodes.norm_label: write_uid — owner-scoped idempotency inside the guard's own uniqueness constraint

nodes.label: Phase 7 regression sweep
nodes.rationale: T7.5.4: 48 agents, five attack lenses over a 17-commit diff, then one independent skeptic per claim told to default to refuted — 42 claimed, 35 survived, 7 refuted.

nodes.label: Nobody has decided the Android hardware back button
nodes.rationale: Measured in the source: @capacitor/app is not a dependency and no backButton listener exists, so the behaviour is Capacitor's default. Back from mid-workout is the row that matters.
nodes.norm_label: nobody has decided the android hardware back button

nodes.label: Keyboard avoidance in WKWebView
nodes.rationale: iOS resizes the visual viewport, not the layout viewport, so a position:fixed bottom bar can sit under the keyboard or float above it wrongly.

nodes.label: Session and cookies across a cold launch
nodes.rationale: The refresh cookie is Path-scoped and SameSite-explicit, and webviews persist cookies differently; this is the failure that looks like 'the app logged me out for no reason'.
nodes.norm_label: session and cookies across a cold launch

nodes.label: The wake lock release path is the half nobody tests
nodes.rationale: A lock that is never released is a battery complaint, so the screen MUST sleep after the workout finishes.
nodes.norm_label: the wake lock release path is the half nobody tests

nodes.label: A durable bearer token outside the archive story
nodes.rationale: The ICS calendar feed token had a revocation column but no expiry and no link to the coach-client row, so archiving a client left a working URL to their schedule.
nodes.norm_label: a durable bearer token outside the archive story

nodes.label: Formula versioning that breaks the thing it protects
nodes.rationale: Storing a formula column beside a stored e1RM and then indexing and comparing without it means changing the formula silently corrupts every comparison.
nodes.norm_label: formula versioning that breaks the thing it protects

nodes.label: Freeze triggers that guard a subset of columns
nodes.rationale: A frozen completed log could still have its plan id, bodyweight and every rollup rewritten, because the trigger listed five columns and the table had twenty.
nodes.norm_label: freeze triggers that guard a subset of columns

nodes.label: CSRF middleware mount order
nodes.rationale: Mounted below health/config and above every API router, so a new router cannot forget to opt in.

nodes.label: Uniform error envelope and ERR codes
nodes.rationale: Always {error, code, requestId}; codes come from ERR in src/lib/http.js and are never invented inline.
nodes.norm_label: uniform error envelope and err codes

nodes.label: An FTS5 external-content index addresses its source by rowid
nodes.rationale: So the source table cannot be WITHOUT ROWID; use a surrogate id plus a UNIQUE index on the natural key.
nodes.norm_label: an fts5 external-content index addresses its source by rowid

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT(col) needs a real constraint on that column
nodes.rationale: users.email is unique only via an index on lower(trim(email)), so INSERT OR IGNORE is the form that works there.
nodes.norm_label: on conflict(col) needs a real constraint on that column

nodes.label: Frontend and backend must share one zod major
nodes.rationale: npm gave the frontend zod 3 while the backend had 4, which kills the shared-schema plan; both are pinned to ^4.
nodes.norm_label: frontend and backend must share one zod major

nodes.label: Piscina strips SQLite errors down to a bare code
nodes.rationale: The worker re-wraps them with the message and the failing statement; the omission cost three blind hunts.
nodes.norm_label: piscina strips sqlite errors down to a bare code

nodes.label: Restart the backend after adding a router
nodes.rationale: New routes 404 until server.js restarts and the frontend's hot reload hides it; this has cost time three separate times.
nodes.norm_label: restart the backend after adding a router

nodes.label: run-server.js is a supervisor — kill it first
nodes.rationale: Killing only server.js makes it respawn, which keeps a lock on data/app.db.
nodes.norm_label: run-server.js is a supervisor — kill it first

nodes.label: Accents ship desaturated one step off their source hue
nodes.rationale: Saturation only, hue and lightness held, so no pack changes identity; a saturated accent buzzes on an OLED panel in a dark room, which is the only room this app runs in.
nodes.norm_label: accents ship desaturated one step off their source hue

nodes.label: The admin sidebar is a grid column, not a second fixed element
nodes.rationale: A fixed rail would have to know about the nav, the safe-area inset and the toast layer: three z-index decisions to get wrong instead of none.
nodes.norm_label: the admin sidebar is a grid column, not a second fixed element

nodes.label: animate-pulse and animate-spin are re-pointed, not banned
nodes.rationale: A rule enforced by deleting the convenient thing gets worked around; the gate reads index.css rather than carrying its own list, so bounce and ping stay build failures until they are re-pointed too.
nodes.norm_label: animate-pulse and animate-spin are re-pointed, not banned

nodes.label: Cards separate by border OR shadow, never both
nodes.rationale: The old build did both; here the answer is border everywhere and shadow is reserved for things that actually float.
nodes.norm_label: cards separate by border or shadow, never both

nodes.label: The card is a convention, not yet a component
nodes.rationale: One class string repeated at 181 call sites consuming none of the four card tokens; surface-1 is a card, surface-2 an inset, surface-3 sheets only, and a tappable card must have a hover or the user cannot tell it is a button.
nodes.norm_label: the card is a convention, not yet a component

nodes.label: Charts of body data are direction="neutral"
nodes.rationale: A green number is the app telling someone which direction their body should go — the easiest way for a fitness app to say something harmful to someone with a disordered relationship to food.
nodes.norm_label: charts of body data are direction="neutral"

nodes.label: Say the consequence before the irreversible action
nodes.rationale: A dialog that only asks 'are you sure' moves the decision without informing it; state what changes, whether it can be undone, and when it takes effect.
nodes.norm_label: say the consequence before the irreversible action

nodes.label: --content-pad-b has exactly one definition
nodes.rationale: The layout pads by it and the workout player subtracts it; they once disagreed by 16px and the page scrolled — and a check button that moves is a check button that records the wrong set.

nodes.label: danger is never styled as primary and never sits in the primary position
nodes.rationale: Destructive and irreversible only, and red even in the monochrome pack because color carries meaning there.
nodes.norm_label: danger is never styled as primary and never sits in the primary position

nodes.label: --duration-ambient is separate from the transition scale
nodes.rationale: Loops are not state changes: a skeleton shimmer never arrives anywhere, and running it at 250ms is a strobe. Naming it is what stops nine screens reaching for Tailwind's 2s pulse.
nodes.norm_label: --duration-ambient is separate from the transition scale

nodes.label: --duration-toast is a dwell, not a transition
nodes.rationale: It is a token because two literals had to agree and neither could see the other — the auto-dismiss timeout and the hairline drawing the time remaining. A drained bar over a toast that is still there is the timer lying about itself.
nodes.norm_label: --duration-toast is a dwell, not a transition

nodes.label: An empty state says what will appear here
nodes.rationale: 'No data' tells the user the app is broken; the pattern is title = the current fact, body = the condition under which it fills, with the recurring 'yet'.
nodes.norm_label: an empty state says what will appear here

nodes.label: An error says what happened, what survived, and what to do
nodes.rationale: The sentence that matters after a failure is 'did I lose my work', so it is answered in the same string. Never a code, never a stack, never 'an error occurred'.
nodes.norm_label: an error says what happened, what survived, and what to do

nodes.label: Explain why you are asking, and mark what is optional
nodes.rationale: Every personal field the app asks for costs trust; naming the use, and naming the cost of skipping it, is what buys it back.
nodes.norm_label: explain why you are asking, and mark what is optional

nodes.label: Field always renders a visible label
nodes.rationale: Placeholder-only labelling disappears the moment the user types; errors sit directly below their field, wired through aria-describedby and role=alert so a screen reader hears them when they appear.
nodes.norm_label: field always renders a visible label

nodes.label: Focus is redrawn, never removed
nodes.rationale: Enforced in the control recipe and in index.css, with the focus ring declared as the theme's own colour so it survives a pack swap.

nodes.label: G1 — four utility names resolve to nothing and the gate cannot see them
nodes.rationale: check-tokens builds its owned stems from --color-* and skips any stem it does not own, so border-line, text-label, text-ok and bg-ok-subtle pass the gate and render as nothing. The durable fix is a symmetric half built from --text-*.
nodes.norm_label: g1 — four utility names resolve to nothing and the gate cannot see them

nodes.label: G2 — --text-3 is below the app's own AA constant
nodes.rationale: 3.80:1 on surface-0 while carrying real data at 11-12px in 175 places, and never checked; both text-2 and text-3 must move together, because raising only text-3 collapses two tiers into one.
nodes.norm_label: g2 — --text-3 is below the app's own aa constant

nodes.label: G3 — no middle step between the accent wash and the filled accent
nodes.rationale: Every other semantic family has a 30% border step, so a selected card must choose between invisible and shouting; the 12% wash measures 1.15:1 while carrying the active tab, today, the selected row and the user's own chat bubble.
nodes.norm_label: g3 — no middle step between the accent wash and the filled accent

nodes.label: G4 — the scale is a grid, not a rhythm, and no component owns the card
nodes.rationale: 87% of gaps are 12px or less so proximity carries no information, and five card tokens have zero consumers while the card is a 181-times-copied class string. A decision no component owns is re-made by whoever is typing.
nodes.norm_label: g4 — the scale is a grid, not a rhythm, and no component owns the card

nodes.label: G5 — semantic families that ship and never render
nodes.rationale: All three toast kinds render the same box with only a 20px icon to tell them apart, on the app's only mutation feedback channel; --info is two uses from being dead weight.
nodes.norm_label: g5 — semantic families that ship and never render

nodes.label: G6 — theme-pack identity that never reaches a screen
nodes.rationale: Border width, control height, glow and brand gradient are declared per pack and consumed by no product screen, so Solar's taller controls, Mono's heavier border and Neon's glow are claims the app does not currently make.
nodes.norm_label: g6 — theme-pack identity that never reaches a screen

nodes.label: G7 — the missing hover edge step (landed)
nodes.rationale: An interactive surface could not strengthen its edge on hover without a raw value or misusing the accent on every hoverable row; --surface-border-strong now ships per pack at roughly twice that pack's hairline.
nodes.norm_label: g7 — the missing hover edge step (landed)

nodes.label: G8 — one missing type step
nodes.rationale: text-body plus font-medium is hand-written 13 times across 10 files for the primary line of a list row — the most repeated text role in the product, patched at the call site because the scale has no 15/22/500 step.

nodes.label: Gate invariants a visual pass must not trip
nodes.rationale: Names, file paths and character windows the gates match on: renaming .screen-x or either safe-area exemption blinds the gate, and an exemption is a written decision rather than 'it looked fine on my laptop'.
nodes.norm_label: gate invariants a visual pass must not trip

nodes.label: The gradient law
nodes.rationale: 2-3 stops, 135 degrees, one gradient surface per screen, same hue family, never behind body text, and explicitly never blue-to-purple — the AI-generic combination that sank the previous build.

nodes.label: The hairline is ~12% and the strong step moves with it
nodes.rationale: At 7% the app's only card separator was under half a shade off the card it bounds; both halves are one decision, because raising the base alone would collapse the hover edge into the resting edge. The pack ordering carries 'Mono has the heaviest border', not the absolute numbers.
nodes.norm_label: the hairline is ~12% and the strong step moves with it

nodes.label: Ink is one color at three opacities
nodes.rationale: Declared as space-separated channels so the three text steps are alphas of it; the previous build froze three opaque hexes and broke the moment text sat on anything but surface-0.
nodes.norm_label: ink is one color at three opacities

nodes.label: Macro overshoot is warning, never danger
nodes.rationale: 300 kcal over target is a normal Tuesday, and the tone of a color is part of what it says.
nodes.norm_label: macro overshoot is warning, never danger

nodes.label: UI motion never exceeds 500ms
nodes.rationale: Press feedback at 100ms because a press must answer immediately; 400ms for sheets because bigger things are allowed to take longer, the eye has further to follow.

nodes.label: 582 exercise translations were French, stored under `hu`
nodes.norm_label: 582 exercise translations were french, stored under `hu`

nodes.label: J2 theme engine — 5 packs, accent picker, gradient builder, contrast guard
nodes.norm_label: j2 theme engine — 5 packs, accent picker, gradient builder, contrast guard

nodes.label: The WCAG accent guard was vacuous — its condition can never fail
nodes.norm_label: the wcag accent guard was vacuous — its condition can never fail

nodes.label: /admin/playground — live pack and variant matrix QA surface
nodes.norm_label: /admin/playground — live pack and variant matrix qa surface

nodes.label: Contrast guard — client computes on-accent, server re-verifies >= 4.5
nodes.norm_label: contrast guard — client computes on-accent, server re-verifies >= 4.5

nodes.label: Pre-paint script in index.html (hashed in CSP)
nodes.rationale: Sets data-theme and custom properties before first paint, so there is no FOUC.
nodes.norm_label: pre-paint script in index.html (hashed in csp)

nodes.label: Structural theming — packs change shape, not just colour
nodes.rationale: Radius, shadow, border and control height are per-pack variants, so a sixth pack is tokens.css plus one assignment.
nodes.norm_label: structural theming — packs change shape, not just colour

nodes.label: Theme engine (F14) — HISTORICAL, the code was deleted 2026-08-04
nodes.norm_label: theme engine (f14) — historical, the code was deleted 2026-08-04

nodes.label: Three token layers: primitives, semantic bridge, component cva maps
nodes.rationale: Only the primitives file may contain hex or px; component variants consume semantic classes only.
nodes.norm_label: three token layers: primitives, semantic bridge, component cva maps

nodes.label: NNN_name.sql applied in filename order, each in one transaction
nodes.source_file: docs/brain/60-Decisions/0001 Numbered migrations via PRAGMA user_version.md
nodes.rationale: The migration sets PRAGMA user_version INSIDE its transaction, because a PRAGMA outside it would persist even on rollback.
nodes.norm_label: nnn_name.sql applied in filename order, each in one transaction

nodes.label: Build-time sha256 manifest of vendor-injected CSS
nodes.source_file: docs/brain/60-Decisions/0003 CSP hash allowlist for vendor styles.md
nodes.rationale: The extractor exits non-zero if a package stops injecting; the manifest is never hand-edited.
nodes.norm_label: build-time sha256 manifest of vendor-injected css

nodes.label: The cross-field guard evaluates the effective POST-UPDATE state
nodes.rationale: Any PUT whose resulting row would be theme='custom' with a NULL config gets 400, so the API has no reachable inconsistent state.
nodes.norm_label: the cross-field guard evaluates the effective post-update state
